req.title: Login sets session on success
req.statement: The system shall set session['user_id'] and redirect to / when POST /auth/login receives a matching username and password.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-008 requires that POST /auth/login with valid credentials returns HTTP 302 to '/' and sets session['user_id']. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — valid username+password yields 302 and session cookie with correct user_id; (2) negative NEG — wrong password yields no redirect and no session mutation; (3) negative NEG — unknown username yields no redirect; (4) BVA — session['user_id'] is exactly the integer id from the fixture (1 for 'test'), not None or another value; (5) STC — after successful login the session persists across a subsequent request. Mutation targets: status code constant (302 vs 200/301), redirect location ('/' vs other), session key name ('user_id'), session value (user['id']), boolean logic in password check, and the session.clear() call.

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Expected /, got {r.headers["Location"]}'
assert b'Incorrect' not in r.data
os.unlink(path)

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_login_valid_credentials_sets_session_user_id():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert 'user_id' in sess, 'session["user_id"] not set'
        assert sess['user_id'] == 1, f'Expected user_id=1, got {sess["user_id"]}'
        assert sess['user_id'] is not None
    os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_login_session_cleared_before_new_session_set
preconditions: Database initialised with both fixture users
Client has a pre-existing stale session with user_id=2
actions: Manually inject session user_id=2 into client session
expected: session['user_id'] equals exactly 1 (old session cleared, new one set)
trace: R-FLASKR-008: session.clear() called before setting new user_id — stale session must not persist
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_login_session_cleared_before_new_session_set():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        sess['user_id'] = 2
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert sess['user_id'] == 1, f'Expected 1 after login as test, got {sess["user_id"]}'
        assert sess['user_id'] != 2
    os.unlink(path)

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_login_get_request_returns_200_not_redirect():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 for GET, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.status_code != 302
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert 'user_id' not in sess
    os.unlink(path)
